Let's think about for a minute:

  • First link is the scientists. Whatever the study they're doing is, the results get bad when scientists are incompetent, closed-minded and/or make a lot of mistakes (or just a single crucial one) when analyzing the data.

  • Next is payment and resources. Usually, scientific studies require a lot of investment on equipment and other stuff. When there are no organizations that are able (or worse: willing) to fund the study, science is severed.

  • Next weak link is the organizations that fund the research, be it a group of people, government or corporation. When they are clearly biased and want to hear only certain results, science will suffer.

If all the previous links work, a proper science can be done. However, for scientific results to reach the general population, there are still a few links:

  • Media is the next link. This link will be weak if media doesn't want to cover the science results or is very sensationalist, often exaggerating the results.

  • Final link is the general population itself. Population also needs to be open to results either because of their values (e.g. religion) or because the previous links have clearly shown weakness.

Any other links I've missed?
Scientific studies are as strong as are their weakest link, especially when results have to reach the audience.
